_doc: Curated compiler-bug corpus for measuring the safety-net's detection power (TS-GAP-006). Each mutant is a targeted, exact, UNIQUE find/replace patch to a real line in a TypeScript compiler source file under packages/runar-compiler/src/. run-mutation.ts applies each patch to the working tree, runs the mapped fast in-process gate(s), records caught-vs-survived, and ALWAYS reverts. Because the gates resolve `runar-compiler`/`runar-testing` through the root vitest SRC alias (see vitest.config.ts), a mutated src file is observed WITHOUT a rebuild. Scope: TS tier only; Go/other-tier mutants are a documented future extension. Six Palmer-class entries (TS-GAP-007 / remediation-plan Phase E1, 2026-08) target packages/runar-compiler/src/passes/{04-anf-lower,05-stack-lower}.ts (branch-merged-locals, inverting 23ef2d2b) and packages/runar-sdk/src/{state,contract}.ts (state-section MINIMALDATA framing, also inverting 23ef2d2b; constructor-slot splice length and codeSeparator off-by-one, new families gated on conformance/sdk-vertical). These four inversion mutants and the two sdk-vertical mutants are gated by packages/runar-testing and packages/runar-sdk VM/unit tests and by conformance/sdk-vertical rather than the compiler-only gates above. Six frame-offset / branch-merge entries (v1 audit mutation-survivor triage, 2026-08-17) were derived MECHANICALLY rather than by hand: 1169 generated mutants over 05-stack-lower.ts, 06-emit.ts and src/optimizer/* were scored against the 71-fixture byte-exact golden corpus (fold-OFF), the 66 survivors in the branch-merge / frame-offset class were re-run against a wider 2101-compile corpus (generated stateless+stateful contracts, every forced branch and loop shape, both folding modes), and the six that changed bytes there are real coverage holes rather than equivalent mutants. Each is killed by a delta-reduced witness pinned in packages/runar-testing/src/__tests__/stack-frame-mutation-pins.test.ts, and each kills exactly the mutants named on it (1:1, measured). The other 60 changed nothing across 2101 compiles; they are recorded as evidence-of-equivalence in the audit report, NOT added here, because a corpus entry that no program can distinguish measures nothing.

_gates.differential-witness: cd conformance && npx vitest run witnesses/differential.test.ts
_gates.fold-equivalence: cd conformance && npx vitest run witnesses/fold-equivalence.test.ts
_gates.peephole-exhaustive: cd packages/runar-compiler && npx vitest run src/__tests__/peephole-exhaustive.test.ts
_gates.fold-execution: cd conformance && npx vitest run witnesses/fold-execution.test.ts
_gates.sdk-vertical-constructor-slots: cd conformance && npx tsx sdk-vertical/runner/vertical-runner.ts --tiers typescript --filter bigint-0
_gates.sdk-vertical-codeseparator: cd conformance && npx tsx sdk-vertical/runner/vertical-runner.ts --tiers typescript --filter codesep-tag-zero

_schema.file: repo-relative path to the compiler src file
_schema.find: exact substring that MUST occur exactly once in file
_schema.class: one of: off-by-one stack index | swapped operands | dropped OP_VERIFY | if-without-else regression | branch-merge regression | state-framing regression | constructor-slot splice regression | codeSeparator off-by-one
_schema.stage: compiler pipeline stage: anf-lower | stack-lower | emit | constant-fold | peephole; or SDK-layer stage: sdk-state | sdk-splice
_schema.expectCaughtBy: gate names that MUST fail (catch) this mutant; empty => documented survivor
_schema.checkGates: for documented survivors: gates run to CONFIRM the mutant survives them
_schema.finding: for documented survivors: the measured coverage hole this mutant records

mutants.finding: Previously a MEASURED HOLE (survivor): no witnessed fixture executed an all-constant subexpression through the fold pass, so a fold arithmetic bug in evalBinOp('+') was invisible to the execution gates. CLOSED by conformance/witnesses/fold-execution.test.ts, whose accept/reject verdict depends on a folded constant (2n + 3n) and is checked by both the source-vs-script differential oracle and the fold-OFF/fold-ON oracle; the mutation now diverges both and is caught.

PALMER-1 inversion, RE-DERIVED 2026-08-06 against 4b0f688f (multi-result branch node). MEASURED per-gate firing (2026-08-06, each gate run separately against the applied patch): branch-merged-locals-vm 5/9 shapes fail (S3 k=2 same-set, S6 k=3, S7 k=2 mixed types, S8 the filed 4-local asymmetric reproducer, S9 nested — S1/S2 k=1 and S4/S5 are untouched by a list truncated to its FIRST entry); real-crypto-branch-merged-locals 1/3 spends fail (the toFirst==0 accept, where the else-arm reassigns nb and na must survive); branch-result-depth-invariant does NOT fire (18/18 still pass) and is deliberately NOT listed — this defect preserves arm depth and corrupts which NAME occupies a slot, and that invariant only sees depth. The previous patch disabled `if (mergedLocals.length >= 2)` inside branchOutputRejectionReason — a function that only runs when an if arm emits an output, which the branch-merged-locals fixtures never do — so it applied cleanly, gated nothing, and SURVIVED while baseline.json recorded it as caught. The current patch truncates collectBranchMergedLocals' canonical merge list to its first entry, so only ONE local ever gets the explicit two-pass copy-then-rebind block both arms need and every other genuinely-reassigned local falls through to undeclared-result machinery — the pre-23ef2d2b behaviour, in the place that now decides it.

PALMER-1 inversion (stack-lower face), RE-DERIVED 2026-08-06 against 4b0f688f. The previous patch added the `_properties` guard to `elseMatchesThenNResultLayout`, which after 4b0f688f is only reachable when nDeclared === 0 — every branch-merged-locals shape now takes the declared-results path instead, so the patch applied to dead code and SURVIVED while baseline.json recorded it as caught. The current patch puts the same pre-23ef2d2b `_properties` membership guard on the decision that replaced it: the by-name adoption of the declared results in lowerIf. A merged LOCAL is then registered under the if-binding's name instead of its own, so the parent's stackMap names a different slot than the one the arms actually left — one stackMap name for N physical results, which is exactly the pre-fix failure. MEASURED per-gate firing (2026-08-06, each gate run separately, twice, against two different working-tree states): branch-merged-locals-vm 8/9 shapes fail (all but S2, the if-without-else shape, which never reaches the declared-results adoption); branch-result-depth-invariant 12/18 fail — unlike its anf-lower peer this face also moves the stale-slot roll-out, so Layer C (7b888035) sees it; real-crypto-branch-merged-locals 3/3 spends fail. All three listed because all three were observed to fire in both runs.

PALMER-2 inversion: re-applies the #110 MINIMALDATA short-circuit (OP_1..OP_16 / OP_1NEGATE) to the STATE section, which the interpreter never executes and the compiler's on-chain reader parses strictly as <len><data>. Verified caught by both state-push-framing-vm.test.ts and c28-state-strict.test.ts.

mutants.finding: PALMER-2 inversion (READ face): re-teaches decodePushData to accept OP_1..OP_16 / OP_1NEGATE as state-section framing. MEASURED GAP: with the encoder left correct, state-push-framing-vm.test.ts's round-trips never construct an OP_N-framed blob, so this mutant SURVIVES that gate alone (verified by execution) -- only c28-state-strict.test.ts's direct `deserializeState(fields, '55')` negative pin catches it. expectCaughtBy lists both because the mutant IS caught overall (c28-state-strict fires); run-mutation.ts's missedExpectedGates reporting flags state-push-framing-vm as the gate that did NOT fire, which is the honest TG-007 finding: that VM test's decode coverage is round-trip-only for this shape (P3 violation) and should gain a direct malformed-input case.

Phase C3 (TG-016) mutant: appends a stray byte to every constructor-slot substitution in buildCodeScript(), so the deployed code part is one byte too long per slot and every subsequent byte offset shifts. Caught by the compiler<->SDK vertical pin (conformance/sdk-vertical), which compares the TS SDK's deployed script against an INDEPENDENTLY re-derived code part (reference/derive.ts, imports nothing from packages/**) -- horizontal 7-SDK agreement alone would not have caught a bug that only one tier's splice logic has. Re-derived 2026-10-14 after N-223 (packages/runar-sdk/src/contract.ts) wrapped this read in `resolveConstructorArg(paramIndex)` for a shared out-of-range guard; the find string `encoded: encodeArg(this.constructorArgs[slot.paramIndex]),` no longer occurred (0x) so the mutant was STALE. Re-pointed at the new call site with the same stray-byte-per-slot fault and re-measured by hand (apply, run the gate with output visible, revert -- not inferred from exit code alone): `cd conformance && npx tsx sdk-vertical/runner/vertical-runner.ts --tiers typescript --filter bigint-0` exits 1 with `[tier:typescript] deployed locking script does not begin with the independently-derived code part (first difference at byte 2: 7b vs 00)` and `[tier:typescript] does not match expected-locking.hex (...)` -- the vertical pin's own SDK-vs-independent-derivation comparison in step [4] of vertical-runner.ts fires, not `[golden]` (step [3], which never touches the SDK and is unaffected by a contract.ts mutation) and not an SDK-side length-guard throw. Same gate, same failure mode as the original 2026-08 measurement.

Phase C4 (TG-016) mutant: off-by-one on the deploy-time-adjusted codeSepIndex value baked into a codeSepIndexSlots placeholder. Caught by the compiler<->SDK vertical pin against the independently-derived expected-code-part.hex / expected-vertical.json for the CodeSepMatrix fixture.
